scope: Independent AI Golden SOP content review of four unselected re-lemma pilot drafts at exact file hashes; no human, media, device or live sign-off.

structuralChecks.sourceProvenance: Every source occurrence ID, marked expression and exact source sentence matches the source inventory; target regex finds the intended form in every cited full source sentence.
structuralChecks.contract: Fresh build followed by --check passes for all 12 drafts: 12 lessons, 72 assessed questions, 48 audio requests, 0 structural review flags.
structuralChecks.replyAndGlossary: Each reply has four options with exactly one target-bearing golden option. All 60 glossary spans re-slice from the actual suggested English answers with only permitted case normalization, and none supplies a target phrase. Pragmatic validity still has the editorial findings listed.
structuralChecks.audio: Each lesson has four distinct requested audio texts with a target match. Audio synthesis, voice, playback and device behavior have not been reviewed.
structuralChecks.content: All seven step surfaces, six answer keys, English/Traditional Chinese choices, two changed-context writing answers, speaking models and target spans were read for sense and fairness.

findings.evidence: Reply asks why Leila avoided boasting about a design award but supplies no Leila scene or visible work. Option a asserts she had shown judges what she built; option d asserts she preferred answering questions only when asked. Neither is given in the prompt or preceding Mina photography scene.
findings.problem: The four “valid” replies are speculative explanations for a new character, so the target-bearing option cannot be judged against a concrete, shared situation.
findings.repair: Ground the prompt in Leila’s completed design being available for judges/others to inspect and her choice to show it instead of boasting. Then write four answers all supported by that scene; remove invented preference in d unless the prompt explicitly establishes it.

findings.evidence: Question asks what the reporter did after confirming several witnesses lied. The listening scene says she checked phone records and traced false timelines; a says she checked dates in each statement, and d says she asked follow-up questions about a contradiction. Those are plausible investigations but are not reported actions.
findings.problem: At least one, and likely two, of the four purportedly valid replies invents what the reporter actually did. The question is past-factual rather than “what could she do”.
findings.repair: Either change the prompt to ask what steps could reasonably help untangle the established lies, or replace a/d with actions directly stated in the scene. Keep all four true for the same time frame and one target-bearing golden reply.

findings.surface: lesson architecture: listening.promptZh, reply.promptEn, scene.promptZh, contrast.promptZh, dialogue.promptZh, speaking.promptZh, writing.promptZh
findings.evidence: Across the seven steps, the learner repeatedly decides whether an unwelcome task recurs/never seems finished versus a one-off finished job. Listening, scene, contrast, dialogue and writing all hinge on fresh batches arriving; reply and speaking restate the same point.
findings.problem: The draft gives too little variation in learner decisions for Golden SOP P85 (“outline seven different learner decisions”), and the highly compositional target “never-ending chore” may not justify a full advanced-expression lesson at this level. This is an editorial scope decision, not a structural-build defect.
findings.repair: Have a human editor decide whether to retain this natural-English item. If retained, redesign distinct steps around repetition versus one long finite job, mildly exasperated register, figurative exaggeration versus literal infinity, whether a task is genuinely unwelcome, and a practical response; keep the original source sense and two changed-context models.

findings.evidence: The register fields name arts criticism, work/performance, investigations, or mildly exasperated description, but do not explicitly identify a likely speaker-listener pair as Golden SOP P81 requests.
findings.problem: The use-context brief is less complete than the adjacent eight Author A lessons; this matters for scaling editorial review and avoiding odd dialogues.
findings.repair: Add a natural likely speaker and listener for each pilot and specify neutral/informal/formal level where not already clear. Do not change keys or target strings solely for metadata.

lessonOutcomes.advanced-native-2341: no new lesson-specific issue; pilot brief metadata remains incomplete
lessonOutcomes.advanced-native-2343: repair reply grounding and pilot brief metadata
lessonOutcomes.advanced-native-2418: repair reply factual validity and pilot brief metadata
lessonOutcomes.advanced-native-2435: human editorial hold on distinctiveness and seven decisions; pilot brief metadata

releaseConclusion: Keep 2343, 2418 and 2435 unselected pending repairs/editorial scope decision; 2341 has no new lesson-specific finding in this review. All four remain provisional pending human and media/device reviews.
